data.gender_notes: Navalkant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Navalkant is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Naval' meaning navel and 'Kanta' meaning lord or protector. This name is believed to symbolize the divine presence within an individual and the protection of the divine being over the physical body. The name Navalkant carries the meaning “Lord of the Navel” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Navalkant usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the navel and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Navalkant Bhagavatula was a renowned mathematician, professor and Indian independence activist from Andhra Pradesh, India. He was the founder of the Indian Mathematical Society in 1931 and served as its first president. He was also a member of the Indian National Congress, and was arrested for his activism during the Quit India Movement in 1942.
historical_references.context: Founder of Indian Mathematical Society and Indian independence activist

historical_references.reference: Navalkant Kaul Shukla was the first Indian-born Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, serving from 1956 to 1960. He was a key figure in the Indian economy in the late 1950s, helping to stabilize the rupee and establish the RBI as an independent central bank.
